results.question: Why do people save items to a wishlist in the first place?
results.restated: What reasons do people give, in public posts and reviews, for saving items to a wishlist on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: This corpus can speak to reasons people SAY they deferred or exited after wishlisting, but it cannot break those reasons into finer, named sub-themes beyond the codes reported here. The most-discussed barriers are the material & digital-physical gap (C2), price (C6), fit & size uncertainty (C1), styling & self-image (C3), and fulfilment concerns (C7) — all framed as shares of discussion, not user behavior [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 records, 226 distinct authors, out of 1018 (share 0.237), across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6): 207 records, 189 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.203), across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 records, 185 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.186), across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 records, 142 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.151), across 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Fulfilment (C7): 140 records, 137 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.138), across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- External validation from reviews/receipts (C4): 82 records, 80 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.081), across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- External validation & social proof (partner/peers) (C10): 68 records, 67 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.067), across 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 54 records, 49 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.053), across 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Action trigger (journey stage) (C13): 51 records, 50 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.05), across 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- Comparison & decision load (C5): 22 records, 22 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.022), across 3 sources; below the minimum-n threshold for ranking by source [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Intent never existed (C9): 21 records, 21 authors, out of 1018 (share 0.021), across 2 sources; below the minimum-n threshold for ranking by source [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Stage shares (context for where defer/exit shows up): Stage C defer 526/1018 (share 0.517); Stage C exit 199/1018 (share 0.195) [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]].

In users' words
- “I kept waiting for a special occasion to wear it.” [[rec|136a736371a446dec9bcdd288488cec6b9db77fb]]
- “I used to buy for the "vibe" but after I realised the amount of clothes I have” [[rec|f25944642b667c3d03053b6c4fda7dec7fb0c41c]]
- “Now I'm wondering if a nice watch makes more sense.” [[rec|33dde1bc8bc5b9b7190dee0fe87a5ddcaa344869]]
- “see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]]

Variation
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12) appears in 42 Reddit records out of 309 (share 0.136), 11 YouTube out of 573 (share 0.019), and 1 App Store out of 22 (share 0.045) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C12]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C12]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C12]].
- Action trigger (C13) appears in 40 Reddit out of 309 (share 0.129), 9 YouTube out of 573 (share 0.016), and 2 Play out of 114 (share 0.018) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C13]].
- External validation from reviews/receipts (C4) appears in 43 YouTube out of 573 (share 0.075), 33 Reddit out of 309 (share 0.107), 3 App Store out of 22 (share 0.136), and 3 Play out of 114 (share 0.026) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]].
- Comparison & decision load (C5) is too thin to report across sources beyond the raw small counts: 12 Reddit out of 309 (share 0.039), 9 YouTube out of 573 (share 0.016), 1 App Store out of 22 (share 0.045) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C5]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C5]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

How much of this reflects “no intent” vs “deferred intent”
- Deferred or stalled intent themes: Action trigger (C13) occurs in 51 records out of 1018 (share 0.05) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]; Intent extinguished after saving (C12) occurs in 54 out of 1018 (share 0.053) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- No intent: Intent never existed (C9) occurs in 21 records out of 1018 (share 0.021) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]].
Interpretation: These are shares of discussion tied to codes, not a partition of saves; the corpus cannot directly label any individual wishlist save as “reference shelving” or “genuine deferred intent” [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].

Do saves cluster with other barriers
- Action trigger (C13) co-occurs with Styling & self-image (C3) in 22 records; lift 2.852 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]].
- Intent extinguished (C12) co-occurs with Styling & self-image (C3) in 22 records; lift 2.693 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]].
- Action trigger (C13) co-occurs with Price (C6) in 20 records; lift 1.929 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2) co-occurs with External validation from reviews/receipts (C4) in 53 records; lift 2.73 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]].
Interpretation: These co-occurrences suggest that stalled or extinguished intent often appears in posts that also discuss style fit, price timing, or seeking review-based reassurance; they remain correlations within discussion, not causal attributions [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].

Which specific sub-themes drive broad reasons
Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of what this is about — there are no validated sub-theme splits beneath codes like Action trigger (C13) or Intent extinguished (C12) to enumerate the “exact motivations” beyond the examples visible in quotes and records [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers in the same stage attract more discussion than post-save intent codes: Material & digital-physical gap (C2) 241/1018 (share 0.237), Price (C6) 207/1018 (share 0.203), Fit & size uncertainty (C1) 189/1018 (share 0.186), Styling & self-image (C3) 154/1018 (share 0.151), and Fulfilment (C7) 140/1018 (share 0.138) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- Several barriers frequently co-occur, indicating that single-cause explanations are incomplete (e.g., C2 with C4 in 53 records; lift 2.73) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]].

Confidence
Medium. The lead codes have substantial record counts and appear across multiple sources, but two validation thresholds failed at the method level, several key codes lack measurable agreement with human labels, and source independence is limited to roughly three types [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- Shares reflect discussion, not shopper behavior or funnel drop-off; no user-level analytics are available [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Two validation thresholds failed; relevance recall is estimated below target and several codes lack measurable reliability with gold labels [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; excluded material likely skews price/value and delivery/trust, so rankings are conditional on this filter [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Stage A is under-detected by construction; forgetting or never revisiting wishlists is unlikely to be posted about [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]].
- Only about 36% of relevant discussion is Myntra-specific; platform-specific inferences rest on a smaller pool [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Segments are derived from classification rules, not observed behaviors; lifts into “undecided” segments are partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Source independence is limited; Google Play and App Store share review dynamics, and Reddit access was indirect [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Small-n codes (e.g., C5, C9) are reportable but not rankable by source beyond raw counts [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
gate_reasons: the corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of what this is about
gate_caveats: whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C5

bad_quotes: genuine deferred intent

results.question: What stops people from buying the things they have saved?
results.restated: What stops people from buying items they have saved to wishlists on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Most wishlist non-purchases are raised at the confidence-check stage (Stage C), led by the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), price (C6), and fit & size uncertainty (C1). Mentions split between deferral and exit depending on the barrier: appearance and fit tend to defer, while price and fulfilment more often read as exits. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1018, Stage C, confidence-phase, outcome=defer, across 4 sources, mean confidence 0.773. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]
- Price (C6): 207 of 1018, Stage C, eliminator-phase, outcome=exit, across 4 sources, mean confidence 0.752. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1018, Stage C, confidence-phase, outcome=defer, across 4 sources, mean confidence 0.816. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1018, Stage C, confidence-phase, outcome=defer, across 3 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]
- Fulfilment (C7): 140 of 1018, Stage C, eliminator-phase, outcome=exit, across 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
- External validation & social proof (C4): 82 of 1018, Stage C, confidence-phase, outcome=defer, across 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]
- External validation & social proof — check with partner (C10): 68 of 1018, Stage C, confidence-phase, outcome=defer, across 3 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]]
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 54 of 1018, Stage C, confidence-phase, outcome=exit, across 3 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]]
- Action trigger (C13): 51 of 1018, Stage C, trigger-phase, outcome=defer, across 3 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]
- Comparison & decision load (C5): 22 of 1018, Stage C, confidence-phase, outcome=defer, across 3 sources; below the minimum N for ranking. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]
- Cost surprise (D1): 14 of 1018, Stage D, eliminator-phase, outcome=exit, across 3 sources; below the minimum N for ranking. [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

Concentration by source (examples)
- C2 appears on Reddit 104 of 309 and YouTube 116 of 573; it is present on app-store reviews as well (Play 18 of 114; App Store 3 of 22). [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]]
- C6 is highly represented in Play reviews 60 of 114, and also appears on Reddit 74 of 309 and YouTube 70 of 573. [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]]
- C1 is most visible on YouTube 144 of 573; it also appears on Reddit 40 of 309. [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]]
- C4 spans YouTube 43 of 573 and Reddit 33 of 309, with smaller counts on app stores. [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]]

Journey stage and outcome
- Stage C dominates: C2 (241 defer), C6 (207 exit), C1 (189 defer), C3 (154 defer), C7 (140 exit), C4 (82 defer), C10 (68 defer), C12 (54 exit), C13 (51 defer). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]
- Stage D is thin: cost surprise (D1) 14 exit. [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]]
- Early-stage chatter exists but is not the focus here: Stage A defer 107 of 1018, Stage A exit 3 of 1018. [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|exit]]

Addressable vs “not live” intent
- Interpretation: The confidence-phase deferrals (e.g., C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C10, C13) read as addressable with better information, guidance, or timing tools, while eliminator exits (e.g., C6, C7) and “intent extinguished after saving” (C12) more often read as non-purchases even if UX improves. Supporting counts: C12 54 exit; C6 207 exit; C7 140 exit. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]

Explicit counterfactuals
- Interpretation: The brief’s records and counts do not surface explicit “I would have bought if X were fixed” statements; the evidence is coded outcomes (defer vs exit) rather than articulated counterfactuals.

Compound reasons (co-occurring pairs)
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2) co-occurs with External validation & social proof (C4): 53 joint records; lift 2.73. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]]
- C2 co-occurs with Fulfilment (C7): 65 joint records; lift 1.961. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]]
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) co-occurs with External validation & social proof — check with partner (C10): 37 joint; lift 2.931. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]]
- Action trigger (C13) co-occurs with Price (C6): 20 joint; lift 1.929. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]]
- A smaller pair suggests a price-plus-other dynamic: C11 with Price (C6): 15 joint; lift 3.074. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C11|C6]]

In users' words
- “My reason was quality” [[rec|af130b9c55ede19f66e4ea81d42c4464d7ac0e31]]
- “the price is also 10x cheaper in india” [[rec|f1c09b668f7e6988c5862e18ab833056b5158be0]]
- “And I'm 5'7, should I buy an overcoat?” [[rec|a91133402e1ca1100b362aaf8833b2d3cb8d6c61]]
- “see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]]

Variation
- By source, price (C6) is especially prominent in Play reviews 60 of 114, with presence on Reddit 74 of 309 and YouTube 70 of 573. [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]]
- The gap between online look and reality (C2) is raised across Reddit 104 of 309 and YouTube 116 of 573, with smaller app-store counts, indicating cross-source presence rather than a single-channel artifact. [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]]
- Fit & size (C1) shows a higher share on YouTube 144 of 573 than on Reddit 40 of 309. [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]]
- Interpretation: The brief notes some items are too thin to order by source for C5 and D1; treat any apparent ordering for these as provisional. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers at the same stage also feature: Styling & self-image (C3) 154 defer, Fulfilment (C7) 140 exit, External validation & social proof — check with partner (C10) 68 defer, Intent extinguished (C12) 54 exit, and Action trigger (C13) 51 defer. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]
- Pairs that rarely appear alone suggest multi-cause stalls (e.g., C2 with C4; C1 with C10), so single-issue fixes may not resolve all deferrals. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]]

Confidence
- Medium. Price (C6) and fit & size (C1) are reliability-cleared (kappa 0.64 and 0.66), while C2’s agreement is weaker (kappa 0.43) and C4/C5/D1 are not measurable on reliability due to small gold pools. Two validation thresholds failed overall, and relevance recall is estimated below target. [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|D1]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]

Limitations
- The corpus measures what people choose to talk about, not funnel behavior; shares are discussion shares, not drop-off or conversion rates. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on this scope. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]
- Only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical findings should be read against this smaller base. [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]
- Source independence is limited to roughly three source types; app-store reviews share a common skew. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]
- Some codes have low Ns or unmeasured reliability (e.g., C5, D1), so they are reportable but not rankable. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]
- Segments derived from codes can circularly reflect confidence-phase definitions; interpret “undecided” lifts with caution. [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]]
- Price (C6) is constrained by a no-monetary-incentive context; prevalence should not be read as a discounting prescription. [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]]
gate_caveats: how often this is raised: too thin to report for D1
an ordering of these barriers: too thin to report for C5, D1
whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C5, D1

results.question: What are people still uncertain about at the moment they decide whether to buy?
results.restated: Which specific uncertainties do people still have at the moment they are deciding whether to buy a saved fashion item?
results.answer:
Answer
Shoppers most often pause over the material & digital-physical gap (C2), price (C6), fit & size uncertainty (C1), styling & self-image (C3), and what recipients actually said (C4) at decision time, with C2 raised in 241 of 1,018 records and C6 in 207 of 1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1,018 records; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6): 207 of 1,018; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1,018; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1,018; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- What recipients said (C4): 82 of 1,018; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- Comparison & decision load (C5): 22 of 1,018; 3 sources; below-minimum-n flag present [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]].
- Co-occurrence (simultaneous doubts), selected pairs:
  - C2 with C4: 53 joint records; lift 2.73 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]].
  - C2 with C7: 65 joint; lift 1.961 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].
  - C1 with C3: 40 joint; lift 1.399 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]].
  - C1 with external validation & social proof (C10): 37 joint; lift 2.931 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]].
  - C6 with journey trigger (C13): 20 joint; lift 1.929 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].
  - C6 with value anchoring (C11): 15 joint; lift 3.074 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C11|C6]].
- “Would have bought if X were resolved” (explicit counterfactuals):
  - Price (C6): 31 of 201 coded C6 records [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]].
  - Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 29 of 232 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C2]].
  - Styling & self-image (C3): 19 of 143 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C3]].
  - What recipients said (C4): 15 of 77 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C4]].
  - Comparison & decision load (C5): 4 of 21 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C5]].
  - Fit & size (C1): 5 of 177 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C1]].
- Sub-themes within fit & size (C1), out of 189 C1-coded records:
  - C1.1: 82 of 189 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.1]].
  - C1.2: 49 of 189 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.2]].
  - C1.3: 25 of 189 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.3]].
  - C1.4: 19 of 189 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.4]].
  - Unclear: 24 of 189 [[analysis_subcode|C1|unclear]].

In users' words
- “significantly less quality when sold in india in comparison to other countries” [[rec|f1c09b668f7e6988c5862e18ab833056b5158be0]].
- “Omggg I was just now adding things to my cart for the B1G1 sale” [[rec|b515b6c496b3bf94f2fba6fd110447c1537ac47c]].
- “Lacoste knows people my size exists. Desi brands don’t. :/” [[rec|a7494a411fbdbf6f9aa9b85f374ad9addc08d8af]].
- “I didn’t like the Korean fit either” [[rec|7d1bb5f6e5dc96671b9228faf0755350783b6269]].

Variation
- Cross-source spread for the leading uncertainties:
  - Material & digital-physical gap (C2): YouTube 116 of 573; Reddit 104 of 309; Play 18 of 114; App Store 3 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]].
  - Fit & size (C1): YouTube 144 of 573; Reddit 40 of 309; Play 3 of 114; App Store 2 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
  - Styling & self-image (C3): Reddit 99 of 309; YouTube 53 of 573; Play 2 of 114 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C3]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C3]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C3]].
  - What recipients said (C4): YouTube 43 of 573; Reddit 33 of 309; App Store 3 of 22; Play 3 of 114 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]].
  - Price (C6): Reddit 74 of 309; YouTube 70 of 573 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]].
- Interpretation: For comparison & decision load (C5), cross-source stability is uncertain given the small total n and a below-minimum-n flag on prevalence; treat any source-level differences as tentative [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]].

Counter-evidence
- Other decision-stage barriers also raised:
  - Fulfilment (returns, C7): 140 of 1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
  - External validation & social proof (C10): 68 of 1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
  - Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 54 of 1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
  - Action trigger (journey stage, C13): 51 of 1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
  - External validation elsewhere (C14): 38 of 1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].
- Some leading uncertainties appear alongside others rather than alone:
  - C2 with C7: 65 joint records (fulfilment concerns paired with digital-physical gap) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].
  - C1 with C10: 37 joint (fit & size with social proof) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]].
  - C2 with C6: 54 joint (material/appearance with price) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C6]].
  - C3 with C6: 23 joint [[analysis_cooccurrence|C3|C6]].

Confidence
Medium. Two high-prevalence codes (C1, C6) have reliable agreement with the human coder (kappa 0.66 and 0.64) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]], but C2 and C3 are marked weak (kappa 0.43 and 0.52) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]], and C4/C5 reliability is not measurable [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]]. Method-wide thresholds failed on two validation checks [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. The sample spans three independent source types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]] with substantial Ns in the top categories [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not user behavior or funnel outcomes; no conversion or abandonment rates exist here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrower than everyday “save-to-buy” talk and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust; rankings are conditional on that screen [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of records are Myntra-specific; most evidence generalizes to Indian fashion shopping rather than Myntra alone [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Source independence is effectively three types (YouTube, Reddit via third-party, app stores), not four; triangulation should be read accordingly [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Segment lifts are partly circular because segments are classification-derived, not observed [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Small-n categories (e.g., C5 with 22 records) are reportable but not rankable; treat cross-source splits and fine-grained claims with caution [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]].
- Agreement with the human coder fails thresholds for some codes and overall validation thresholds failed; treat orderings that rely on weak/not-measurable codes as provisional [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]].

results.question: How do people compare the items they have shortlisted?
results.restated: How do shoppers compare multiple items they have shortlisted on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: Shoppers describe ad‑hoc, effortful comparisons rather than a consistent, platform‑supported flow: side‑by‑side outfit building appears in wish‑list comparisons, and some users cross‑check prices off‑platform and prioritise items with buyer photos/reviews — but the corpus holds nothing on how much of the opportunity this represents.

Evidence
- Mentions of Comparison & decision load appear on Reddit (12 of 309) and YouTube (9 of 573), with a lone App Store mention (1 of 22); these counts are small and uneven across sources [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C5]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C5]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C5]].
- Off‑platform price checks are explicitly described: “Always compare with Myntra” [[rec|18c4a3dbcb3c9eab8751f4dd693bc060df14644e]].
- A side‑by‑side, mix‑and‑match workflow is requested: “compare outfits side by side, make our own outfit set by selecting multiple other things like tshirt , bottoms etc and swe them visually in order.” [[rec|cab273eb219679fce34fbdf92480c4933bbdc486]].
- Reviews with real‑world photos are used to decide among options: “only order those dresses which have a good number of reviews and pictures of people wearing them under normal lighting” [[rec|dbffa7fbae654d2154241949c2072f7078c94bc1]].

In users' words
- “If we could just compare outfits side by side, make our own outfit set by selecting multiple other things like tshirt , bottoms etc and swe them visually in order.” [[rec|cab273eb219679fce34fbdf92480c4933bbdc486]]
- “Always compare with Myntra” [[rec|18c4a3dbcb3c9eab8751f4dd693bc060df14644e]]
- “Always always always only order those dresses which have a good number of reviews and pictures of people wearing them under normal lighting” [[rec|dbffa7fbae654d2154241949c2072f7078c94bc1]]

Variation
- Interpretation: The source split for Comparison & decision load is too thin to support a stable cross‑source read; the counts are below common reporting floors, so a single‑platform signal could be misleading [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C5]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C5]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C5]], [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]], [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Counter-evidence
- Other, rival barriers dominate the same stage of discussion, suggesting many shoppers focus on different blockers than comparison mechanics: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears in 241 of 1018, fulfilment (C7) in 140 of 1018, external validation & social proof (C10) in 68 of 1018, intent extinguished after saving (C12) in 54 of 1018, and action trigger (C13) in 51 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].

Confidence
- Low. Comparison & decision load has very few records and its reliability is not measurable; only 1 gold label carried this code, so agreement statistics are unavailable [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]], [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]. Source triangulation is limited by only three independent source types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- The corpus measures what people say, not what they do; any shares reported are shares of discussion, not conversion or drop‑off rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under‑captures price/value and delivery‑trust material; rankings are conditional on that filter [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Counts for Comparison & decision load are below common floors, constraining ordering and generalisation [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Reliability is unknown for Comparison & decision load (not enough gold labels) and weak for some adjacent codes, so any dependency on those is provisional [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]].
- Only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra‑specific; most evidence reflects Indian online fashion shopping generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on how much of the opportunity side‑by‑side or off‑platform comparison represents in the overall save‑to‑purchase journey.
gate_reasons: the corpus holds nothing on how much of the opportunity this represents
gate_caveats: whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C5

results.question: Are people who wishlist actually intending to buy, or just bookmarking?
results.restated: Among people who save items to wishlists on Indian online fashion platforms, how many are genuinely intending to buy later versus merely bookmarking or shelving items without purchase intent?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The corpus shows both bookmark-like use and real purchase intent around wishlists, but it cannot speak to differences between kinds of shopper. Bookmarking without live intent appears explicitly, yet there is substantial discussion of triggers, counterfactuals and workarounds that imply intent to buy later.

Evidence
- Bookmarking/no intent:
  - C9 — intent never existed: 21 out of 1018 relevant records (share 0.021) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]].
  - Segment ① Collectors — saving as a taste archive: 126 out of 1018 relevant records (share 0.124) [[analysis_addressable|collectors]].
- Intent that fades after saving:
  - C12 — intent extinguished after saving: 54 out of 1018 (share 0.053) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Explicit counterfactuals (users saying they would have bought if a barrier were removed):
  - Action trigger (C13): 12 counterfactuals out of 49 coded instances (share 0.245) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C13]].
  - Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 8 counterfactuals out of 52 coded instances (share 0.154) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C12]].
  - Intent never existed (C9): 0 counterfactuals out of 20 coded instances (share 0) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C9]].
- Workarounds that indicate sustained intent:
  - External validation & social proof (C4): 17 with workarounds out of 77 coded instances (share 0.221) [[analysis_workaround|C4]].
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 17 with workarounds out of 177 coded instances (share 0.096) [[analysis_workaround|C1]].
  - Intent never existed (C9): 0 with workarounds out of 20 coded instances (share 0) [[analysis_workaround|C9]].

In users' words
- “i went to their brick n mortar store because of the same sizing issue” [[rec|dff1e8c42ec7425a8260683d42a33b842ef9265c]].
- “first see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get and then go ahead” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]].
- “I was cleaning my wishlist yesterday and realised half the clothes I save are not for anything I actually have planned” [[rec|6102d72a4134c75fd1e23e0da192954f39145fbd]].
- “shoes size eppadi online lea purchase pannurathu” [[rec|88de0264a0bfbce32ecfd1d5c99129fd39bdfb38]].

Variation
- By source platform:
  - Intent extinguished after saving (C12) is discussed on Reddit more often than YouTube: 42 out of 309 on Reddit (share 0.136) vs 11 out of 573 on YouTube (share 0.019) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C12]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C12]].
  - Action trigger (C13) shows a similar pattern: 40 out of 309 on Reddit (share 0.129) vs 9 out of 573 on YouTube (share 0.016) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C13]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C13]].
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1) is raised more on YouTube than Reddit: 144 out of 573 (share 0.251) vs 40 out of 309 (share 0.129) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]].
- Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on how this differs between kinds of shopper; segments are derived, not observed [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are widely discussed, consistent with deferred-but-intended purchases rather than mere bookmarking:
  - Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 out of 1018 (share 0.237) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
  - Price (C6): 207 out of 1018 (share 0.203) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
  - Styling & self-image (C3): 154 out of 1018 (share 0.151) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
  - Fulfilment (C7): 140 out of 1018 (share 0.138) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
  - External validation & social proof (C10): 68 out of 1018 (share 0.067) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Co-occurrence shows barriers do not act in isolation, pointing to ongoing decision-making rather than absence of intent:
  - Action trigger (C13) co-occurs with Styling & self-image (C3): 22 joint records, lift 2.852 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]].
  - Action trigger (C13) co-occurs with Price (C6): 20 joint records, lift 1.929 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].
  - Material & digital-physical gap (C2) co-occurs with External validation & social proof (C4): 53 joint records, lift 2.73 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]].

Confidence
- Medium. One core code (Fit & size uncertainty, C1) is reliable with kappa 0.657 [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]]. However, key intent-signalling codes have unknown reliability (C13 and C4 not measurable) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]]. Two validation thresholds fail overall [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. The corpus is sizeable at 1018 relevant records [[analysis_addressable|corpus]].

Limitations
- Shares here are of discussion, not behaviour; no funnel or conversion data exist [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; recall is estimated at about 79% and excluded material skews toward price/value and delivery/trust, so rankings are conditional on what was included [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Silent forgetting is under-detected; a low count of non-reconsideration cannot be read as rarity [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]].
- Only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra-specific; most evidence is about Indian online fashion generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Segments are derived from classifications rather than observed shopper types, so the corpus cannot separate differences between kinds of shopper [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- App-store sources are not independent types; effectively three independent source types are represented [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Counts below common floors should not be over-interpreted; some codes and pairings sit near those thresholds [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

results.question: Do different kinds of shoppers get stuck in different ways?
results.restated: Do different shopper segments (kinds of shoppers) get stuck on different barriers when deciding whether to buy items saved to a wishlist on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Yes — different shopper segments talk about different barriers when deciding whether to buy wishlist items, with clear contrasts: for example, Committed Waiters are dominated by Price (C6), while Stuck Deciders concentrate on the material & digital-physical gap (C2) and fit & size uncertainty (C1), and Lapsed Intenders are led by Intent extinguished after saving (C12) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]]. Interpretation: all shares below are shares of discussion, not conversion.

Evidence
- Segment definitions and sizes (records in each segment):
  - Stuck Deciders: n=392; top barriers include the material & digital-physical gap (C2 n=167/392), fit & size uncertainty (C1 n=159/392), styling & self-image (C3 n=94/392), and fulfilment (C7 n=62/392) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C1]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C3]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C7]].
  - Ready Buyers: n=198; fulfilment (C7 n=39/198) is present alongside activation themes (A-codes) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|3]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|3|C7]].
  - Hesitant Waiters: n=108; Price (C6 n=77/108), the material & digital-physical gap (C2 n=59/108), styling & self-image (C3 n=38/108), fit & size uncertainty (C1 n=24/108), and fulfilment (C7 n=15/108) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C3]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C1]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C7]].
  - Lapsed Intenders: n=78; Intent extinguished after saving (C12 n=54/78) and C11 are most distinctive; price (C6 n=22/78), styling & self-image (C3 n=22/78), fulfilment (C7 n=18/78), and the material & digital-physical gap (C2 n=15/78) also appear [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C3]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C7]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C2]].
  - Committed Waiters: n=116; Price (C6 n=108/116) dominates; fulfilment (C7 n=6/116) also occurs [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|5|C6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|5|C7]].
- Distinctiveness (lifts within segments):
  - Stuck Deciders: most distinctive barriers are External validation & social proof (C10), fit & size uncertainty (C1), and External validation & social proof (C4) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]].
  - Hesitant Waiters: most distinctive barriers are C8, Action trigger (C13), and Price (C6) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|6]].
  - Lapsed Intenders: most distinctive are Intent extinguished after saving (C12), C11, and styling & self-image (C3) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]].
  - Committed Waiters: most distinctive is Price (C6) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]].
  - Ready Buyers: distinctives are activation themes (A3.2, A1.1, A2.2); fulfilment (C7 n=39/198) is present but not listed as distinctive [[analysis_segment_recommendation|3]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|3|C7]].
- Source-level context (to gauge skew when comparing segments):
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1) is discussed more on YouTube (n=144/573) than Reddit (n=40/309) and the Play Store (n=3/114) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]].
  - The material & digital-physical gap (C2) is discussed on Reddit (n=104/309) and YouTube (n=116/573) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]].
  - Price (C6) shows strong discussion on the Play Store (n=60/114) and Reddit (n=74/309) [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]].

In users' words
- “there are sizing variations and differences in quality between the different colours” [[rec|8a2701c85c668f294af3abb28f4581d32c085656]].
- “knowing whether to proceed with the purchase or wait” [[rec|2bc41c195f4019216b2c91e477307858beb5e8f6]].

Variation
- Segment-level contrasts (what stands out most to whom):
  - Stuck Deciders concentrate on the material & digital-physical gap (C2 n=167/392) and fit & size uncertainty (C1 n=159/392); both are also among this segment’s most distinctive barriers (C1 and C10/C4) [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C1]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]].
  - Hesitant Waiters emphasise Price (C6 n=77/108) alongside the material & digital-physical gap (C2 n=59/108) and styling & self-image (C3 n=38/108); C8 and Action trigger (C13) are especially distinctive here [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C3]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|6]].

  - Committed Waiters overwhelmingly discuss Price (C6 n=108/116) [[analysis_segment_code_v2|5|C6]].
  - Ready Buyers show fulfilment (C7 n=39/198) among their top codes, though their most distinctive features are activation themes (A-codes) rather than barriers [[analysis_segment_code_v2|3|C7]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|3]].
- Interpretation: Whether these between-segment differences survive any one source (e.g., Reddit vs YouTube) cannot be directly tested here because the brief does not provide segment-by-source breakdowns.

Counter-evidence
- Other barriers also show up in the same decision stage across the corpus: External validation & social proof (C4 n=82/1018), External validation & social proof (C10 n=68/1018), Intent extinguished after saving (C12 n=54/1018), Action trigger (C13 n=51/1018), and External validation & social proof (C14 n=38/1018) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]].
- Barriers often co-occur, suggesting compound problems: for example, the material & digital-physical gap with External validation & social proof (C2 with C4, n_joint=53; lift=2.73), and fit & size uncertainty with External validation & social proof (C1 with C10, n_joint=37; lift=2.931) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]].

Confidence
- Medium. Larger segments (e.g., Stuck Deciders n=392) provide robust counts, and key codes like fit & size uncertainty (C1) and price (C6) are reliability-rated “reliable” (kappa 0.66 and 0.64) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]]. However, major contributors like the material & digital-physical gap (C2) and styling & self-image (C3) have “weak” agreement (kappa 0.43 and 0.52) and some smaller segments have only one rankable cell, so code-level detail there is directional [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]].

Limitations
- Interpretation: Segments are derived from the classification, not observed, so higher lifts for undecided-stage barriers in undecided segments are partly circular and should not be over-read as causal structure [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- The instrument measures discussion, not behaviour — no funnel or conversion data is present [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery-and-trust material; rankings are conditional on that scope [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Agreement thresholds: two validation thresholds fail at the corpus level; relevance recall is estimated at about 79%, and only 2 of 5 measurable codes clear kappa 0.60 [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Source independence is limited; Play and App Store share review-skew, and Reddit was collected via a third-party; triangulation is across roughly three independent source types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Platform specificity: only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical interpretations should be made cautiously [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Minimum-n floors apply: in some segments only one code cell meets n>=30, so code-level detail there is directional rather than rankable [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]].
- Constraint on C6: price is large but out-of-scope for monetary solutions; any action should focus on transparency, anchoring, and timing rather than discounts [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].
- Too thin to report for C5 by segment and by source: Comparison & decision load (C5) is sparse across segments (e.g., Stuck Deciders n=12/392; Hesitant Waiters n=8/108; Lapsed Intenders n=2/78) and across sources, so mention rather than rank [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C5]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C5]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C5]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C5]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C5]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C5]].

How segments are defined (and sample adequacy)
- Segments are named cohorts constructed from segment-by-code or segment-by-stage classifications with stated sizes: Stuck Deciders (n=392), Ready Buyers (n=198), Hesitant Waiters (n=108), Lapsed Intenders (n=78), Committed Waiters (n=116) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|3]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|6]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]]. Interpretation: The brief does not supply total distinct-author counts per segment; it reports distinct authors for specific code-by-segment cells (e.g., Stuck Deciders C2 has n_distinct_authors=161), so author-level deduplication at the segment total cannot be verified here [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C2]].

What would contradict segment differences
- Interpretation: If top barriers (e.g., Price C6, material & digital-physical gap C2, fit & size C1) appeared at roughly similar shares across all segments, that would argue for homogeneity; the present segment rows instead show different top codes and distinctives (e.g., Committed Waiters: C6 n=108/116 vs Stuck Deciders: C2 n=167/392 and C1 n=159/392), supporting difference rather than uniformity [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|5|C6]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|4|C1]].

results.question: Given that most people never intended to buy, is the wishlist worth fixing?
results.restated: If a large share of wishlist saves were made by people who never intended to buy, would investing in fixing the wishlist user experience be a worthwhile product opportunity?
results.answer:
Answer
Correction: The corpus cannot support “most saves were never intended to buy” because it measures discussion frequency, not shopper rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]. Within that constraint, there is explicit discussion of saving with no live intent (C9), but it is a small counted slice of the corpus (21 of 1018) and is excluded from the addressable opportunity [[analysis_addressable|c9_no_live_intent]].

Evidence
- How often “never intended to buy” is raised: C9 — 21 of 1018 relevant records; reported to size “how much wishlisting is not intent,” then excluded from the opportunity [[analysis_addressable|c9_no_live_intent]].
- Addressable population after excluding non-intent segments: 892 of 1018 records [[analysis_addressable|addressable]].
- Counterfactuals (people saying they would have bought if a specific barrier were removed):
  - Action trigger (journey stage, C13): 12 counterfactuals out of 49 C13-coded records [[analysis_counterfactuals|C13]].
  - External validation & social proof (reviews, C4): 15 of 77 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C4]].
  - Price (C6): 31 of 201 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]].
  - Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 8 of 52 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C12]].
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 5 of 177 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C1]].
  - Intent never existed (C9): 0 of 20 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C9]].
- Workarounds (intent survives barriers):
  - Reviews (C4): 17 of 77 with workarounds; mean_effort=1.941; intensity_index=0.429 [[analysis_workaround|C4]].
  - Price (C6): 30 of 201; mean_effort=1.6; intensity_index=0.239 [[analysis_workaround|C6]].
  - Fit & size (C1): 17 of 177; mean_effort=1.412; intensity_index=0.136 [[analysis_workaround|C1]].
  - Intent never existed (C9): 0 of 20 [[analysis_workaround|C9]].
- Specific, addressable barriers (stage C) and their sizes in this corpus:
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1): n=189; ranked 2 by opportunity score [[analysis_opportunity|C1]].
  - External validation & social proof (reviews, C4): n=82; ranked 4 [[analysis_opportunity|C4]].
  - Price (C6): n=207; ranked 8; flagged as not directly solvable with money [[analysis_opportunity|C6]][[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].
  - Fulfilment (returns pain, C7): n=140; ranked 7 [[analysis_opportunity|C7]].
  - Action trigger (C13): n=51; ranked 9 [[analysis_opportunity|C13]].
  - Comparison & decision load (C5): n=22; scored but below the n>=30 floor for ranking [[analysis_opportunity|C5]][[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Other high-prevalence rival barriers at confidence stage:
  - Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
  - Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Stage outcomes (whether people say they defer or exit at the consideration stage):
  - Consideration (stage C): 526 defer, 199 exit, 20 not stated; denominator=1018 [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]][[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]][[analysis_stage_outcome|C|na]].

In users' words
- “I usually just wait since your phone has captured the data that you are looking for a specific product. It’ll eventually show up in multiple sites.” [[rec|653385bf09973ea5d85a71d673720b4158169736]]
- “I have never seen even one thing i like at Zudio, but I can’t go into Marks and Spencer’s pick up my size and walk out without even trying it on because i know it will fit.” [[rec|8dc9f620df57ba31889994d52e9f60eddacf3fd3]]
- “3 star is for most of the images not being the same as shown in pictures. solution read product reviews then buy.” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]]
- “I was cleaning my wishlist yesterday and realised half the clothes I save are not for anything I actually have planned…” [[rec|6102d72a4134c75fd1e23e0da192954f39145fbd]]

Variation
- By source, fit & size (C1) is discussed on YouTube (144 of 573) and Reddit (40 of 309), with smaller app-store footprints (3 of 114 on Play; 2 of 22 on App Store) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]][[analysis_source_code|play|C1]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Price (C6) is raised across Reddit (74 of 309), YouTube (70 of 573), and is especially prominent in Play reviews (60 of 114) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]][[analysis_source_code|play|C6]].
- Reviews/social proof (C4) appears on YouTube (43 of 573), Reddit (33 of 309), with smaller app-store mentions (3 of 22 App Store; 3 of 114 Play) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]][[analysis_source_code|play|C4]].
- Intent extinguished (C12) is more visible on Reddit (42 of 309) than YouTube (11 of 573) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C12]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C12]].
Interpretation: These patterns suggest the findings are not driven by a single source type, but app-store data have their own skew and are not independent of each other [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Counter-evidence
- Other barriers compete at the same stage: material & digital-physical gap (C2) with 241 of 1018, styling & self-image (C3) with 154 of 1018, fulfilment (C7) with 140 of 1018, and external validation via friends/partners (C10) with 68 of 1018 also appear in the same consideration phase [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Barriers often co-occur: fit & size (C1) with social validation (C10) at n_joint=37; reviews (C4) with the digital-physical gap (C2) at n_joint=53; action trigger (C13) with price (C6) at n_joint=20; intent extinguished (C12) with styling (C3) at n_joint=22 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]].
- Stage outcomes show both defer and exit at consideration; wishlist UX alone would be competing with eliminators like fulfilment (C7) that drive exits [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]][[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].

Confidence
Medium. The corpus is sizable (1018 records) and key codes like fit & size (C1) and price (C6) have reliable agreement with a human coder (kappa 0.657 and 0.645) [[analysis_addressable|corpus]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]]. However, several relevant codes (C4, C13) are not measurable for reliability, and two validation thresholds fail at the metric level [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]][[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- Discussion is a proxy, not a funnel: all shares are how often people talk about a barrier, not how often shoppers actually drop off or convert [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Stage A under-detection: forgetting or never re-opening a wishlist is unlikely to be posted about, so early-stage misses are probably undercounted [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]].
- Narrow relevance rubric: recall is estimated to skew away from price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on that narrower slice [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Platform specificity: only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical conclusions for Myntra rest on a smaller subset [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Reliability: per-code agreement is strong for C1 and C6 but unknown for C4 and C13; two validation thresholds fail [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]][[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Source independence: Google Play and App Store are not independent types and carry review-skew; Reddit access is via a third party [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Monetary constraints: price (C6) is prominent but explicitly out of scope to solve via discounts; any recommendation must focus on transparency, timing, or anchoring [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].
- Segment caveat: segments are derived from codes, not observed behavior; any lift into “undecided” is partly definitional [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Minimum-n floors: claims for low-n codes (e.g., C5 with n=22) are not rankable [[analysis_opportunity|C5]][[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

results.question: Since the analysis proves that discounts are the fix, how big should they be?

results.answer: The premise that discounts are definitively “the fix” is not supported here. This engine only contains public discussion of barriers people say they face when moving from saving to buying on Indian online fashion platforms; it does not include transaction or funnel data and can’t estimate how large a discount should be or the lift per percentage point. It also cannot isolate decisive effects for a given item or separate discount effects from fit, trust, or delivery factors. Answering your question would require item- and user-level purchase data linked to shown discount levels, checkout pricing components, and outcomes, ideally from controlled experiments or price-elasticity analyses.

results.question: Why did you only look at Myntra reviews?
results.restated: Did this analysis only use Myntra reviews, and if not, which sources and platforms does the corpus cover?
results.answer:
**Answer**
This engine was built as a five-stage pipeline over public feedback, and every
number it reports is a count of discussion rather than a measure of behaviour.

**Evidence**
- Records were collected from YouTube, Reddit, Google Play and the App Store,
  plus a small set of URL-verified published research. Everything collected was
  kept; exclusions are marked rather than deleted, so the exclusion log is
  browsable in the Data Bank.
- Each record was scored for relevance, then classified against a frozen
  codebook of 34 barrier codes across four journey stages. Every code
  assignment carries an evidence span checked to be an exact substring of the
  original text.
- In parallel, records were clustered with no sight of the codebook, so themes
  could emerge that the codebook did not anticipate.
- The classifier was validated against 108 records labelled by hand. Those
  results, including the two thresholds that FAIL, are published in full under
  Analysis → Validation.
- Answers here are assembled by choosing from a fixed set of queries, retrieving
  verbatim records, deliberately retrieving evidence AGAINST the emerging
  answer, and then checking every number and quote in the finished text against
  what was actually retrieved.

**Confidence**
High — this describes the pipeline, not a finding. The specific reliability of
any individual number is reported with that number.

**Limitations**
Interpretation: the honest summary is that this engine is a hypothesis
prioritiser built on what people chose to say in public. It is designed to point
interviews at the right questions, not to settle them.

Answer
Partial: The corpus does not contain evidence about wishlist “vanishing.” The closest related discussion is the availability at decision time (C8), where people say items or sizes aren’t available when they want them [[analysis_code_prevalence|C8]].

Evidence

In users' words

Counter-evidence
- Other barriers are discussed more often than C8. Material & digital-physical gap (C2) appears in 241 of 1018 records [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], Price (C6) in 207 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]], Fit & size uncertainty (C1) in 189 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]], Styling & self-image (C3) in 154 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]], and Fulfilment (C7) in 140 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].

Source independence is limited (app stores share similar skews) [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

results.question: What does the data say about reverse-chronological wishlist ordering?
results.restated: What evidence does the corpus contain about reverse-chronological wishlist ordering (newest-first) and its effects on shoppers' ability to rediscover, act on, or manage saved items?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The corpus contains no direct mentions of wishlist ordering (reverse‑chronological/newest‑first), so we cannot say how ordering affects rediscovery or action; the evidence only supports adjacent barriers after saving, not ordering mechanics. Mentions of Intent extinguished after saving (n=54 of 1018) and Action trigger (journey stage) (n=51 of 1018) point to post‑save drop‑off in discussion, but not specifically due to how wishlists are ordered [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].

Evidence
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12): n=54 of 1018; 49 distinct authors; from 3 sources; mean_confidence=0.596 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Action trigger (journey stage) (C13): n=51 of 1018; 50 distinct authors; from 3 sources; mean_confidence=0.49 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- Availability at decision time (C8): n=35 of 1018; 35 distinct authors; from 4 sources; mean_confidence=0.764 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C8]].
- Comparison & decision load (C5): n=22 of 1018; 22 distinct authors; from 3 sources; mean_confidence=0.525 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]].
- Co‑occurrence suggests that after‑save barriers often appear with styling and price concerns, but again not tied to ordering: C12 with Styling & self‑image (n_joint=22; lift=2.693); C13 with Styling & self‑image (n_joint=22; lift=2.852); C13 with Price (n_joint=20; lift=1.929) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].

In users' words
- “Tough to break until I get much older” [[rec|d3b91ce5f456601fe1cd3969cedcd125a392d33d]].
- “I’d rather buy one pair of jeans I love than keep replacing cheaper ones every few months” [[rec|747a3b2cd0e0bbd817d88cdcfb18828ae9000f93]].
- “Not sure why but most of the items are not deliverable to Gujarat” [[rec|9de4f2d715e1caa5a324c20648130166f3f23442]].
- “Why not use Google Lens? It scans the outfit and gives you both identical options (if available) as well as similar items with shopping links and sometimes price comparisons.” [[rec|1a6511608caf1d4a9fbacf4746940f920219741f]].

Variation
Interpretation: The corpus does not isolate wishlist ordering at all, so we cannot break out whether ordering concerns occur on specific sources or segments. For adjacent after‑save barriers, source mix exists but is not about ordering: for C12, Reddit n=42 of 309, YouTube n=11 of 573, App Store n=1 of 22; for C13, Reddit n=40 of 309, YouTube n=9 of 573, Play Store n=2 of 114 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C12]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C12]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C12]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C13]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C13]]. Interpretation: As flagged, evidence is too thin to assess cross‑source robustness for C13, C8, and C5 in the specific context of ordering.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers dominate discussion and could explain post‑save inaction without invoking wishlist ordering: Material & digital‑physical gap (n=241 of 1018), Price (n=207), Fit & size uncertainty (n=189), Styling & self‑image (n=154), Fulfilment (n=140) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- After‑save barriers rarely appear in isolation: C13 co‑occurs with Styling & self‑image and Price above chance; C12 co‑occurs with Styling & self‑image, indicating intertwined causes rather than a single ordering issue [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]].

Confidence
Low. There are zero direct mentions of wishlist ordering; reliability for key adjacent codes (C13, C5, C8) is not measurable on gold labels; two validation thresholds fail at the metric level; and source independence is limited [[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C8]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]] [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- Proxy, not behavior: all shares are discussion shares, not funnel outcomes; no user‑level or conversion data exists here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Narrow relevance: the rubric under‑captures some decision‑relevant topics; rankings reflect a narrowed slice of discussion [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Under‑detection of forgetting: silent Stage A problems (no re‑entry) are inherently less posted about, so absence of ordering mentions may reflect posting dynamics, not true absence [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]].
- Reliability: per‑code agreement is not measurable for several adjacent codes; two validation thresholds fail [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Source independence: app stores are not independent; Reddit data was third‑party collected; effectively three source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Platform specificity: only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra‑specific; mechanical in‑app conclusions for Myntra rest on a smaller base [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Minimum‑n floor: thin categories cannot be confidently ranked; absence of ordering mentions may be a data‑volume artifact [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Segments are derived, not observed; any segment inferences around undecided users are partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].

Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of wishlist ordering concerns (e.g., pinning, sorting, newest burying older items), nor on workarounds tied to ordering.

results.question: What about price?
results.restated: How does price (and related value/cost concerns) figure among the reasons people do not buy items they saved to wishlists on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The corpus shows that price (Price [C6]) is a commonly raised reason in discussion about not proceeding from wishlist to purchase, but the corpus holds nothing on whether people abandon or merely postpone.

Evidence
- Price (C6) appears in 207 of 1018 records (share 0.203; 189 distinct authors; 4 sources) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Cost surprise (D1) appears in 14 of 1018 records (share 0.014; 14 distinct authors; 3 sources) [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]].
- By source for Price (C6):
  - Google Play: 60 of 114 (share 0.526) [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]].
  - Reddit: 74 of 309 (share 0.239) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]].
  - App Store: 3 of 22 (share 0.136) [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]].
  - YouTube: 70 of 573 (share 0.122) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]].
- By source for Cost surprise (D1):
  - Google Play: 8 of 114 (share 0.07) [[analysis_source_code|play|D1]].
  - YouTube: 5 of 573 (share 0.009) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D1]].
  - Reddit: 1 of 309 (share 0.003) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D1]].
- Specific price issues reflected:
  - Perceived overpricing/value doubts (Price [C6]): “Price Are Slightly Higher than other platforms” [[rec|83f902cade59dd75d0914095fcae5638b5ab90ae]]; “you can always verify you have always paid higher than what is the real value of the product” [[rec|4ebe300f22d19e33a8aa2d3d54bd3e2dc4e85585]].
  - Comparison-driven shopping (Comparison & decision load [C5] with Price [C6]): “gives you both identical options (if available) as well as similar items with shopping links and sometimes price comparisons” [[rec|1a6511608caf1d4a9fbacf4746940f920219741f]].
  - Cost surprise (D1) is present in 14 of 1018 records [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]].
- Co-occurrence suggesting compound friction:
  - Price (C6) with Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 54 joint records (lift 1.102) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C6]].
  - Price (C6) with Fulfilment (C7): 21 joint records (lift 0.738) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C6|C7]].
  - Material & digital-physical gap (C2) with Fulfilment (C7): 65 joint records (lift 1.961) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].
- Explicit counterfactuals (“I would have bought if price were fixed”):
  - Price (C6): 31 counterfactuals out of 201 coded instances (share 0.154; exemplar IDs provided) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]].
  - Cost surprise (D1): 3 counterfactuals out of 14 coded instances (share 0.214) [[analysis_counterfactuals|D1]].
- Workarounds for managing price:
  - Price (C6): 30 of 201 records mention a workaround (share 0.149); mean effort 1.6; intensity index 0.239 [[analysis_workaround|C6]].
  - Example workaround: using Google Lens for “price comparisons” [[rec|1a6511608caf1d4a9fbacf4746940f920219741f]].

In users' words
- “Price Are Slightly Higher than other platforms” [[rec|83f902cade59dd75d0914095fcae5638b5ab90ae]].
- “you can always verify you have always paid higher than what is the real value of the product” [[rec|4ebe300f22d19e33a8aa2d3d54bd3e2dc4e85585]].
- “gives you both identical options (if available) as well as similar items with shopping links and sometimes price comparisons” [[rec|1a6511608caf1d4a9fbacf4746940f920219741f]].
- “I ordered 5 Libas sarees at an offer price... Later, Myntra automatically cancelled them...” [[rec|c9255b2dc886715ba1ac41455a61c11b67ee76aa]].

Variation
- Price (C6) is raised across all sources, with the highest share on Google Play (60 of 114; share 0.526), followed by Reddit (74 of 309; share 0.239), the App Store (3 of 22; share 0.136), and YouTube (70 of 573; share 0.122) [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]].
- Interpretation: The brief is too thin to report whether this holds up across sources for D1, C5, C4, and C7.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are also prominent in the same stage: Material & digital-physical gap (C2) appears in 241 of 1018 (share 0.237), Fit & size uncertainty (C1) in 189 of 1018 (share 0.186), Styling & self-image (C3) in 154 of 1018 (share 0.151), External validation & social proof (C10) in 68 of 1018 (share 0.067), and Intent extinguished after saving (C12) in 54 of 1018 (share 0.053) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2) frequently co-occurs with External validation & social proof (C4): 53 joint records (lift 2.73) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]]. This indicates other, non-price frictions are often discussed alongside or instead of price.

Confidence
- Medium. Price (C6) is marked reliable (agreement 0.864; kappa 0.645) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]], but other relevant codes (D1, C7, C4, C5) are not measurable for reliability [[analysis_gold_agreement|D1]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]]. Two validation thresholds fail at the metric level [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. Source types are only roughly three independent types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- Interpretation: The corpus measures discussion shares, not user actions or funnel outcomes; it cannot say whether wishlist items were abandoned or merely postponed [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; barrier rankings are conditional on this rubric [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical insights rest on a smaller pool [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Two validation thresholds fail; per-code reliability is limited outside C6 [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- For Cost surprise (D1), counts are below the floor for ranking (n=14), so it is reportable but not rankable [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]][[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]].
- Segments (e.g., “undecided”) are derived from codes and are not observed behavior [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Price (C6) is a constrained lever for product teams in this project; it should be interpreted through transparency/timing rather than discounts [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].

whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for D1, C5, C4, C7
