results.question: And how does that split by segment?
results.restated: How do the reasons people don't buy the items they saved to wishlists split by shopper segment?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: This is a segment-level read of what people said blocked wishlist-to-purchase; the corpus does not hold what else comes up alongside these, so it cannot report “what typically co-appears with each barrier inside a segment.”

Evidence
- Stuck Deciders (n=392; 43.9% of the addressable population): the most-discussed barriers are the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) at 167/392, fit & size uncertainty (C1) at 159/392, styling & self-image (C3) at 94/392, external validation & social proof — what did people who actually received it say? (C4) at 64/392, and fulfilment (C7) at 62/392 [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]].
- Hesitant Waiters (n=108; 12.1%): price (C6) at 77/108, the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) at 59/108, styling & self-image (C3) at 38/108, action trigger (C13) at 27/108, fit & size uncertainty (C1) at 24/108, external validation & social proof — what did people who actually received it say? (C4) at 15/108, fulfilment (C7) at 15/108, and comparison & decision load (C5) at 8/108 [[analysis_segment_recommendation|6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C1]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C4]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C7]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|6|C5]].
- Committed Waiters (n=116; 13.0%): price (C6) at 108/116 and fulfilment (C7) at 6/116; action trigger (C13) at 12/116 and external validation & social proof — go check this properly somewhere else (C8) at 12/116 also appear in this segment’s ranking [[analysis_segment_code_v2|5|C6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|5|C7]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]].
- Lapsed Intenders (n=78; 8.7%): intent extinguished after saving (C12) at 54/78, external validation & social proof (C11) at 24/78, price (C6) at 22/78, styling & self-image (C3) at 22/78, fulfilment (C7) at 18/78, the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) at 15/78, fit & size uncertainty (C1) at 6/78, external validation & social proof — what did people who actually received it say? (C4) at 3/78, and comparison & decision load (C5) at 2/78 [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C6]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C7]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C2]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C1]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C4]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|2|C5]].
- Ready Buyers (n=198; 22.2%): fulfilment (C7) at 39/198 is present in this segment’s code-level data [[analysis_segment_recommendation|3]] [[analysis_segment_code_v2|3|C7]].

In users' words
- “cheap rate” and “One more site is there from there you can buy cheap rate of this brand” [[rec|bfbda683b25a54124e8d1b58865051ddf2371fd5]].
- “go for a large size” [[rec|cef46918a6a090928ac6fd50d8b897c72899dad1]].
- “Bought highlander sneakers once, torn within a week.” [[rec|3b11a09390d23a0f98df8f2632203d366cfdfc0e]].
- “It’ll not come within 1k but it’ll last many years.” [[rec|c9fa89f54f676ed99018e1ddb73e34f2add5add1]].

Variation
- By segment: Stuck Deciders concentrate on the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) at 167/392 and fit & size uncertainty (C1) at 159/392, while Hesitant and Committed Waiters surface price (C6) at 77/108 and 108/116 respectively; Lapsed Intenders uniquely show intent extinguished after saving (C12) at 54/78 [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|6]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|5]] [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]].
- By source (overall, not within segments): the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears on Reddit at 104/309 and on YouTube at 116/573; fit & size uncertainty (C1) appears on YouTube at 144/573 and on Reddit at 40/309; fulfilment (C7) appears on YouTube at 67/573 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C7]].
- Interpretation: The corpus was not broken down finely enough to separate whether any segment’s barrier is driven by one forum; there is no segment-by-source table to test source concentration within a segment.

Counter-evidence
- Other barriers people raised in the same stage: styling & self-image (C3) at 154/1018, external validation & social proof — check with partner (C10) at 68/1018, intent extinguished after saving (C12) at 54/1018, action trigger (C13) at 51/1018, and external validation & social proof — go check this properly somewhere else (C14) at 38/1018, all as shares of discussion, not behavior [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]] [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Several barriers co-occur above chance, indicating they often appear together when people post: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) with external validation & social proof — what did people who actually received it say? (C4) at 53 joint records; C2 with fulfilment (C7) at 65; fit & size uncertainty (C1) with external validation & social proof — check with partner (C10) at 37; and action trigger (C13) with price (C6) at 20 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].

Confidence
- Interpretation: Confidence is mixed. The leading segment-specific counts are large (e.g., Stuck Deciders n=392 and Hesitant Waiters n=108), but some key codes vary in reliability.
- Reliable: fit & size uncertainty (C1) shows agreement with the human coder (kappa 0.657), and price (C6) shows agreement (kappa 0.645) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]].
- Weaker/unknown: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) is marked weak (kappa 0.427), and external validation & social proof — what did people who actually received it say? (C4), fulfilment (C7), and comparison & decision load (C5) are not measurable for reliability in this sample [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]].
- Source diversity at the corpus level is present (e.g., C2 appears across four sources), but app stores are not independent from each other as a type [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]. Overall quality thresholds did not fully pass (recall estimated at about 79%; only 2 of 5 codes surpass kappa 0.60) [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not funnel behavior; no user- or conversion-level data exist here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Segments are derived from the very codes they summarize; lifts into undecided segments are partly circular rather than observed associations [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; a hand-read sample suggested excluded material skews toward price/value and delivery-and-trust, so rankings are conditional on what the rubric kept [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of relevant posts are Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical readings rest on a smaller pool [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Some code-level reliability is weak or not measurable, and two validation thresholds failed; treat orderings that depend on those codes as provisional [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Counts below 30 are reportable but not rankable; several segment-by-code cells (e.g., small C5 and C4 cells) should be read as directional [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Price is constrained by “no monetary incentives”; high C6 share should be addressed via transparency, anchoring, and timing rather than discounts [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].

Interpretation: What would contradict a segment-specific finding here?
- If a barrier shows high co-occurrence with a trigger or workaround (e.g., action trigger C13 appearing alongside price C6 at 20 joint records), it suggests intent may survive despite the barrier, weakening a claim that the barrier is decisive within a segment [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].

results.question: Which of those is easiest to fix without a discount?
results.restated: Which wishlist-to-purchase barrier is easiest to fix without offering a price discount?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The material & digital-physical gap (C2) is the easiest non-discount lever to move first — it combines the top opportunity score, is flagged as solvable without money, appears often in discussion, and has concrete “I would have bought if X were fixed” testimony.

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): rank=1, score=0.819, n=241; solvable_without_money=1 [[analysis_opportunity|C2]]. Counterfactuals: 29 of 232 records explicitly say they would have bought if this changed [[analysis_counterfactuals|C2]]. Workarounds: 30 of 232 show users trying to bridge it; mean_effort=1.9 [[analysis_workaround|C2]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): rank=2, score=0.797, n=189; solvable_without_money=1 [[analysis_opportunity|C1]]. Counterfactuals: 5 of 177 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C1]]. Workarounds: 17 of 177; mean_effort=1.412 [[analysis_workaround|C1]].
- External validation & social proof (C4): rank=4, score=0.72, n=82; solvable_without_money=1 [[analysis_opportunity|C4]]. Counterfactuals: 15 of 77 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C4]]. Workarounds: 17 of 77; mean_effort=1.941 [[analysis_workaround|C4]].
- Action trigger (journey stage) (C13): rank=9, score=0.506, n=51; solvable_without_money=1 [[analysis_opportunity|C13]]. Counterfactuals: 12 of 49 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C13]]. Workarounds: 11 of 49; mean_effort=1.364 [[analysis_workaround|C13]].
- Comparison & decision load (C5): n=22; flagged as solvable_without_money=1 but below the floor for ranking [[analysis_opportunity|C5]]. Counterfactuals: 4 of 21 [[analysis_counterfactuals|C5]]. Workarounds: 6 of 21; mean_effort=1.167 [[analysis_workaround|C5]].
- Mechanical friction (D2): n=22; below the floor for ranking [[analysis_opportunity|D2]]. Counterfactuals: 6 of 21 [[analysis_counterfactuals|D2]]. Workarounds: 1 of 21; mean_effort=2 [[analysis_workaround|D2]].

In users' words
- “cheap quality clothes” [[rec|e5dea1941521a6905da935d6e01799adbc1ed584]] (C2)
- “pick up my size” [[rec|8dc9f620df57ba31889994d52e9f60eddacf3fd3]] (C1)
- “you can always verify you have always paid higher than what is the real value of the product” [[rec|4ebe300f22d19e33a8aa2d3d54bd3e2dc4e85585]] (C4)
- “we can buy another dress in same price range” [[rec|ba4d67eb593d2a741cfb697a26e52fad442ce46d]] (C13, C2)

Variation
- Source spread for C2: YouTube n=116 of 573, Reddit n=104 of 309, Play n=18 of 114, App Store n=3 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]].

- Source spread for C4: YouTube n=43 of 573, Reddit n=33 of 309, Play n=3 of 114, App Store n=3 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]].
- Interpretation: For C5 and D2, cross-source robustness is too thin to report beyond the small-n indications named above.

Counter-evidence
- Other barriers are also prominent in discussion: Price (C6) n=207 of 1018 (share=0.203) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]; Styling & self-image (C3) n=154 of 1018 (share=0.151) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]; Fulfilment (C7) n=140 of 1018 (share=0.138) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]; External validation & social proof (distinct construct C10) n=68 of 1018 (share=0.067) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]]; Intent extinguished after saving (C12) n=54 of 1018 (share=0.053) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Causes cluster: C2 co-occurs with C4 in 53 records and with C7 in 65, indicating it rarely appears in isolation [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]]. C1 often appears with C10 in 37 records and with C3 in 40 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]]. C13 appears with C3 in 22 and with C6 in 20 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].

Confidence
Medium. C1 is reliable (kappa 0.657) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]]. C2 underpins the recommendation but has weaker agreement (kappa 0.427) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]]. For C4, C5, C13, and D2, reliability is not measurable on gold labels [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D2]]. Method-wide thresholds are reported as failing, and every share here is discussion, not behavior [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]], [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].

Limitations
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery-and-trust topics; rankings are conditional on that filter [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- These are shares of online discussion, not shopper actions or conversion metrics; no funnel data exists here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Only about 36% of discussion is Myntra-specific; platform mechanics should be read against a smaller base [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- App-store sources are not independent of each other; triangulation spans roughly three source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Some codes have small-n evidence below ranking floors (e.g., C5, D2), so those signals are directionally informative but not orderable [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Classifier reliability is mixed; per-code agreement clears threshold for 2 of 5 measurable codes, and overall validation thresholds are reported as failing [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]].

results.question: Show me what people actually said about it.

results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The corpus does contain many verbatim posts about the gap called Fit & size uncertainty (C1), but it does not show how well-supported this is beyond shares of discussion. Below are the exact things people said, plus how broad the quote pool is and where it comes from.

Evidence
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) appears in 189 of 1018 records, from 185 distinct authors, across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- By source: YouTube 144/573 (143 distinct authors) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]]; Reddit 40/309 (37 distinct authors) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]]; Google Play 3/114 (3 distinct authors) [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]]; App Store 2/22 (2 distinct authors) [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Sub-code counts (names not provided in the brief): C1.1 = 82 of 189; C1.2 = 49 of 189; C1.3 = 25 of 189; unclear = 24 of 189; C1.4 = 19 of 189 [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.1]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.2]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.3]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|unclear]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.4]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) is often mentioned alongside Styling & self-image (C3) with 40 joint mentions, and also with External validation & social proof (C4) with 17 joint mentions [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C4]].

In users' words
- "Boxy fit ko kitne size me pahnana chahie bolo bhai" [[rec|b72066dbb3f70bc31cb0f73e6e4b9188e90594a0]]
- "Bhai mujhe mera size pata nahi kya karu 😢 hight ka hesab sa bata do na XL,XXL ??? Mera 5 fit 6 inc ??" [[rec|ab1bd5e62511b69d3a3b4333652d4a8fe286ed0e]]
- "no i went to their brick n mortar store because of the same sizing issue. levi's jeans are labelled smaller than the actual size...and also..one jean that would have fit u properly at a particular size, at the same size another jeans may not fit u." [[rec|dff1e8c42ec7425a8260683d42a33b842ef9265c]]
- "I have a similar build with wider thighs - Slim fit just hugs whereas straight/relaxed fit is too baggy around the ankles." [[rec|d8296dfee3083d097c09d0bf9b433bd8f4bd669d]]
- "dyeing it changes the size and nature of the fabric." [[rec|5e0a4bac31b341dfd628b9503ad604110e9b6621]]
- "Accessories have problems as the size shown in 3 products that I bought was wrong" [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]]

Variation
- Source mix is broad: C1 appears across YouTube, Reddit, Google Play, and the App Store, with n_sources=4 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]. YouTube contributes 144 records (143 distinct authors), Reddit 40 (37), Play 3 (3), and App Store 2 (2) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Interpretation: The sub-themes of measurement questions, inconsistent sizing across items/colours, body-shape or fit-type matching, and “size shown” issues are present in the quotes above, but the brief does not map these to named subcodes; only counts for unnamed subcodes are provided [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.1]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.2]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.3]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|unclear]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.4]].

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are discussed at least as much or more in this stage: Material & digital-physical gap (C2) 241/1018; Price (C6) 207/1018; Styling & self-image (C3) 154/1018; Fulfilment (C7) 140/1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) is not isolated: it co-occurs with Styling & self-image (C3) and External validation & social proof (C4) above chance, indicating posts often raise multiple doubts together [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C4]].
- At least one user reports easy mitigation via exchange: "the exchange is so far effortless provided you do not loose the tags of the outfit" [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]].
- Interpretation: A pattern of many posts saying returns/exchanges make sizing risk trivial would weaken the case that C1 is a meaningful hesitation; this corpus shows some such language but not in volume quantified beyond the single example cited above.

Confidence
- Medium. The C1 classifier shows reliable agreement with a human coder (kappa 0.657; verdict=reliable) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]], and the pool is sizable (189 records; 185 distinct authors; 4 sources) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]. However, method flags record that two validation thresholds failed and recall is estimated below target [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]], and source independence is limited to roughly three types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- This corpus measures what people chose to post, not what they did in a purchase funnel [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Only about 36% of relevant material is Myntra-specific; much discussion is about Indian fashion e-commerce generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; on a hand-read sample it likely excluded decision-relevant posts, especially about price and delivery/trust, affecting barrier ranking [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Segments are derived from classification, not observed behaviour; any lift into “undecided” segments is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Two validation thresholds failed (kappa target met for some codes but overall thresholds not passed), and recall is estimated, not measured [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- App-store sources share a common bias and Reddit was collected via a third party; there are roughly three independent source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Interpretation: The brief provides counts for C1 subcodes but not their names or definitions, so we cannot map sub-theme labels to subcode IDs beyond illustrative quotes [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.1]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.2]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.3]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|unclear]] [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.4]].

results.question: Is that reliable?
results.restated: Is the count of records that mention approval from someone else (code C10) reliable?
results.answer:
**Answer**
This engine was built as a five-stage pipeline over public feedback, and every
number it reports is a count of discussion rather than a measure of behaviour.

**Evidence**
- Records were collected from YouTube, Reddit, Google Play and the App Store,
  plus a small set of URL-verified published research. Everything collected was
  kept; exclusions are marked rather than deleted, so the exclusion log is
  browsable in the Data Bank.
- Each record was scored for relevance, then classified against a frozen
  codebook of 34 barrier codes across four journey stages. Every code
  assignment carries an evidence span checked to be an exact substring of the
  original text.
- In parallel, records were clustered with no sight of the codebook, so themes
  could emerge that the codebook did not anticipate.
- The classifier was validated against 108 records labelled by hand. Those
  results, including the two thresholds that FAIL, are published in full under
  Analysis → Validation.
- Answers here are assembled by choosing from a fixed set of queries, retrieving
  verbatim records, deliberately retrieving evidence AGAINST the emerging
  answer, and then checking every number and quote in the finished text against
  what was actually retrieved.

**Confidence**
High — this describes the pipeline, not a finding. The specific reliability of
any individual number is reported with that number.

**Limitations**
Interpretation: the honest summary is that this engine is a hypothesis
prioritiser built on what people chose to say in public. It is designed to point
interviews at the right questions, not to settle them.

premise.asserts: There is a count of records mentioning approval from someone else (C10).

results.answer:
Answer
People most often talked about not buying wishlisted items because of the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), price (C6), and fit & size uncertainty (C1), largely at the item‑decision stage rather than at wishlist UX or checkout. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]]

Evidence
- Journey stage mix of the discussion: Stage C (item decision) accounts for 526 of 1018 defer outcomes and 199 of 1018 exit outcomes; Stage B has 21 of 1018 defer and 8 of 1018 exit; Stage D has 50 of 1018 exit; Stage A has 107 of 1018 defer and 3 of 1018 exit. [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|D|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|exit]]
- Top barriers in the Stage C discussion: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears in 241 of 1018 records; price (C6) in 207 of 1018; fit & size uncertainty (C1) in 189 of 1018; styling & self-image (C3) in 154 of 1018; fulfilment (C7) in 140 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
- Intent still live vs extinguished: defer at Stage C is 526 of 1018; exit at Stage C is 199 of 1018; intent extinguished after saving (C12) is 54 of 1018. [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]]
- Source spread for the top barriers: C2 is present in YouTube (116 of 573), Reddit (104 of 309), Play (18 of 114), and App Store (3 of 22). C6 is present in Reddit (74 of 309), YouTube (70 of 573), Play (60 of 114), and App Store (3 of 22). C1 is present in YouTube (144 of 573), Reddit (40 of 309), Play (3 of 114), and App Store (2 of 22). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]]
- How many records discuss wishlist abandonment vs other wishlist uses: Interpretation: the counts here are by journey stage and barrier, not by wishlist‑specific intent types, so the corpus does not separate “wishlist abandonment” from “reference shelf” or “never‑intent” at the counting level given. No FACT row reports that split.

In users' words
- “I kept that purse in wishlist so we could buy that purse on a sale or something.” [[rec|9b26643264276659111220430e855970f5f9169a]]
- “Which size u were in jeans and top ?” [[rec|6dc1c0995889d71ef60d108e5c4810b40ee86e6b]]

Variation
- By source type: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears across all four sources, with Reddit showing 104 of 309 and YouTube 116 of 573; price (C6) appears across all four, with Play showing 60 of 114; fit & size uncertainty (C1) is heaviest on YouTube at 144 of 573. [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]]
- By journey stage: most discussion clusters at Stage C, with 526 of 1018 defer and 199 of 1018 exit, compared with Stage B at 21 of 1018 defer and 8 of 1018 exit. [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|exit]]
- Whether users state they would have bought if the barrier were removed vs workaround: Interpretation: explicit “I would have bought if X” statements are scarce in the retrieved records; price‑timing workarounds do appear (e.g., using wishlist until a sale). [[rec|9b26643264276659111220430e855970f5f9169a]]

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers in the same stage: styling & self-image (C3) is present in 154 of 1018; fulfilment (C7) in 140 of 1018; external validation & social proof (C4) in 82 of 1018; external validation & social proof (C10) in 68 of 1018; intent extinguished after saving (C12) in 54 of 1018. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]]
- Barriers often co-occur, suggesting no single cause dominates within a record: C2 with C4 co-occur in 53 records; C2 with C7 in 65; C1 with C10 in 37; C13 with C6 in 20; C13 with C3 in 22. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]]

Confidence
Medium. Fit & size uncertainty (C1) and price (C6) clear the agreement threshold with the human coder (kappa 0.657 and 0.645), while the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) is weaker (kappa 0.427). Two validation thresholds fail at the corpus level, and estimated relevance recall is about 79% against an 85% threshold. [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not behavioral conversion or abandonment rates; no funnel data exists. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]
- The relevance rubric is narrow; excluded material skews toward price/value and delivery/trust, so barrier rankings reflect this scope. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]
- Stage A (forgetting/no re‑entry) is under‑detected by construction; a low Stage A count is not evidence the phenomenon is small. [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]]
- Only about 36% of the relevant corpus is Myntra‑specific; platform‑mechanical inferences rest on a smaller pool. [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]
- App‑store sources are not independent of each other; effectively three independent source types, not four. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]
- Price (C6) is a major barrier that project constraints forbid solving via monetary incentives; interpret it in terms of transparency, anchoring, and timing. [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]]
- Segments are derived from codes, not observed; lifts into “undecided” are partly circular. [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]]
- Counts below minimum Ns are less stable; treat thin codes cautiously. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]
- Agreement on C2 is below threshold; any ordering that depends on it is provisional. Two validation thresholds fail overall. [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]

results.question: क्या साइज़ को लेकर अनिश्चितता सबसे बड़ी वजह है?
results.restated: Is fit & size uncertainty (code C1) the largest single barrier raised in the corpus about why saved wishlist items are not bought?
results.answer:
Answer
No. The material & digital-physical gap (C2) is raised most often, with price (C6) next; fit & size uncertainty (C1) ranks third in the relevant discussion [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].

Evidence
- Overall prevalence (item-decision stage): C2 n=241 of 1018 (share=0.237); C6 n=207 of 1018 (share=0.203); C1 n=189 of 1018 (share=0.186) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- Other notable barriers (same stage): C3 n=154 of 1018 (share=0.151); C7 n=140 of 1018 (share=0.138); C4 n=82 of 1018 (share=0.081) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- By source for C1: YouTube n=144 of 573 (share=0.251); Reddit n=40 of 309 (share=0.129); Play n=3 of 114 (share=0.026); App Store n=2 of 22 (share=0.091) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- By source for C2 (for comparison): YouTube n=116 of 573 (share=0.202); Reddit n=104 of 309 (share=0.337); Play n=18 of 114 (share=0.158); App Store n=3 of 22 (share=0.136) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]].
- Robustness to weighting: Under perturbation, C2 is top in 0.996 of draws (mean_rank=1.004); C1 is top in 0.004 of draws (mean_rank=1.996) [[analysis_weight_sensitivity|C2]] [[analysis_weight_sensitivity|C1]].

In users' words
- “Which size u were in jeans and top ?” [[rec|6dc1c0995889d71ef60d108e5c4810b40ee86e6b]]
- “And the difference isn’t visible on the hanger. It shows up only when you wear it.” [[rec|7da7de1a996e937c2dc91a995f8f2402f23e8818]]
- “I got this top in 400 🙂 thoda sa wait karna chahiye tha.. 🤧” [[rec|87211e918e956fea232afdf0cfa15bdb37cfbea2]]
- “no return or exchange option” [[rec|893ede648353cc8d160309de57577ec7530ce63a]]

Variation
- By source: C1’s share is higher on YouTube (n=144 of 573; share=0.251) and lower on Play (n=3 of 114; share=0.026), while C2’s share is especially high on Reddit (n=104 of 309; share=0.337). This indicates that C1 does not dominate across sources and that C2’s lead is not driven by a single platform [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]].
- Interpretation: All prevalence rows cited are for the item-decision stage (C); a stage-restricted view does not change the ranking shown here because the reported counts are already stage C.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are frequently raised: styling & self-image (C3) n=154 of 1018 (share=0.151) and fulfilment (C7) n=140 of 1018 (share=0.138) also account for substantial shares of discussion, which counters the idea that C1 is singularly dominant [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- Co-occurrence suggests mixed causes: C1 often appears with external validation & social proof (C10) with n_joint=37 of 1018 (lift=2.931), and with styling & self-image (C3) with n_joint=40 of 1018 (lift=1.399), indicating that fit concerns are intertwined with other doubts rather than standing alone [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]].

Confidence
Medium. C1 and C6 are reliability-cleared (kappa 0.657 and 0.645), but C2 — the top-ranked barrier — has weaker agreement (kappa 0.427), so an ordering that depends on C2 is provisional [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]]. Weight-sensitivity strongly favors C2 as top (top_share=0.996), which supports the conclusion despite C2’s weaker kappa [[analysis_weight_sensitivity|C2]].

Limitations
- The corpus measures shares of discussion, not user behavior or funnel outcomes [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; excluded material likely skews toward price/value and delivery/trust, so rankings are conditional on what was included [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of relevant records are Myntra-specific; findings reflect Indian online fashion generally, not Myntra alone [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Source independence is limited to roughly three types (YouTube, Reddit via third-party, app stores), so cross-source triangulation is constrained [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Two validation thresholds failed overall; per-code agreement is mixed, and only some codes clear the reliability bar [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Segments are derived from classification; any segment lift for confidence-phase codes is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Small-n floors limit rankability of thinner codes; some lower-prevalence barriers cannot be confidently ordered [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- For C6, project constraints prohibit monetary incentives; its prominence should not be read as an argument for price cuts [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].

results.question: Wishlist ka sabse bada problem kya hai aur kitne log bolte hain?
results.restated: What is the single biggest problem people report about wishlists on Indian online fashion platforms, and how many distinct people raise that problem in the corpus?
results.answer:
Answer
Partial: The single biggest problem people raise is the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2 (PHYSICAL-VS-DIGITAL GAP)), with 226 distinct authors raising it; we can report the top problem and its counts, but this corpus cannot support co-occurrence analysis or source/stage robustness checks for several codes because the needed per-slice record minimums are not met, and there is no evidence on what else is mentioned alongside it. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]; [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

Evidence
- Top problem and “how many people”: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2 (PHYSICAL-VS-DIGITAL GAP)) appears in 241 records out of 1018, from 226 distinct authors, across 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]
- Close rivals in the same stage: price (C6 (VALUE & PRICE UNCERTAINTY)) 207 records, 189 distinct authors; fit & size (C1 (FIT & SIZE UNCERTAINTY)) 189 records, 185 distinct authors; styling & self-image (C3) 154 records, 142 distinct authors; fulfilment (C7) 140 records, 137 distinct authors. All out of 1018 records. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]; [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]; [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]; [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
- Source distribution for the top problem (C2): YouTube 116 records out of 573; Reddit 104 out of 309; Google Play 18 out of 114; App Store 3 out of 22. [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]]; [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]]; [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]]; [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]]
- Corpus size and stage context: total 1018 records. Stage C has 526 defer and 199 exit outcomes; Stage A has 107 defer and 3 exit; Stage B has 21 defer and 8 exit; Stage D has 50 exit. [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]]; [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]]; [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|defer]]; [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|exit]]; [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|defer]]; [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|exit]]; [[analysis_stage_outcome|D|exit]]

Variation
- By source: The top problem (C2 (PHYSICAL-VS-DIGITAL GAP)) is raised on all four sources: YouTube 116/573, Reddit 104/309, Google Play 18/114, App Store 3/22. [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]]; [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]]; [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]]; [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]]
- By journey stage: The evidence for the top problem is observed at Stage C. Overall, Stage C carries the largest volume in the corpus (526 defer; 199 exit), so findings are mainly concentrated there. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]; [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]]; [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]]
- Interpretation: The corpus does not provide a corpus-level count of distinct authors across all records; only per-code and per-source distinct-author counts are available.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers at the same stage are also common: price (C6 (VALUE & PRICE UNCERTAINTY)) 207/1018; fit & size (C1 (FIT & SIZE UNCERTAINTY)) 189/1018; styling & self-image (C3) 154/1018; fulfilment (C7) 140/1018. These could challenge the top spot if their counts exceeded C2 in future data. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]; [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]; [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]; [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
- Unclassified residual posts exist but do not present specific wishlist barriers, so they do not disconfirm or support the ranking. [[rec|5702069c2cb13c86b2a51463fb70317b1b68de73]]; [[rec|71b49323bdf1fe903aceac3f1866f5a516c9f406]]; [[rec|c16a154be6e73ee360d753e03657810828768b5d]]

Confidence
Medium. The top problem has substantial counts and appears across four labeled sources (C2: 241 records; 226 distinct authors), which supports stability, but validation thresholds fail (per-code agreement and recall), and the corpus represents roughly three independent source types rather than four. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]; [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]; [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not behavior. The counts measure how often people raise a barrier in public posts, not how often shoppers actually drop off after wishlisting. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]
- Narrow relevance rubric. The ranking is conditional on a narrow inclusion rule that under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; results may shift under a broader definition. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]
- Reliability thresholds failed. Per-code Cohen’s kappa clears 0.60 for only 2 of 5 measurable codes, and relevance recall is estimated at about 79% vs an 85% threshold. [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]
- Stage A under-detected by construction, so a low Stage A count does not imply a small real-world effect. [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]]
- Source independence is limited: Google Play and App Store share review skew, and Reddit access constraints mean about three independent source types. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]
- Platform specificity: only about 36% of relevant material is Myntra-specific; findings generalize to Indian online fashion shopping rather than to Myntra alone. [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]
- Segment caveat: any segment-level lift tied to confidence-phase codes is partly circular, since segments are derived from classification rather than observed. [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]]
- Thin-slice gaps (Route: PARTIAL): The corpus does not meet minimum per-slice counts to detail how often this is raised for several codes and stages (including A (NEVER RECONSIDERED), C1 (FIT & SIZE UNCERTAINTY), C2 (PHYSICAL-VS-DIGITAL GAP), C4 (REAL-BUYER EVIDENCE INSUFFICIENT), C5 (COMPARISON PARALYSIS), C6 (VALUE & PRICE UNCERTAINTY)) or to assert cross-source robustness for those slices; and it contains no evidence on what else co-occurs with the top problem. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

results.question: What do people say about ignoring instructions in their reviews?
results.restated: What do people in the corpus say about ignoring product, care, or seller instructions in their reviews and comments?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The corpus does not directly surface “ignoring product/care/seller instructions” as a distinct theme; instead, people more often discuss adjacent barriers like the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), price (C6), fulfilment/returns friction (C7), and, less often, late-revealed terms (D3). Any finer breakdown of which instructions are ignored vs missing is not available in this corpus.

Evidence
- The gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears in 241 of 1,018 records, from 226 distinct authors, across 4 sources (share 0.237) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6) appears in 207 of 1,018 records, from 189 distinct authors, across 4 sources (share 0.203) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fulfilment (C7) appears in 140 of 1,018 records, from 137 distinct authors, across 4 sources (share 0.138) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- Late-revealed terms (D3) appears in 26 of 1,018 records, from 26 distinct authors, across 4 sources (share 0.026) [[analysis_code_prevalence|D3]].
- Source mix for D3 shows Google Play 13 of 114 (share 0.114), YouTube 6 of 573 (share 0.01), Reddit 6 of 309 (share 0.019), App Store 1 of 22 (share 0.045) [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D3]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D3]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D3]].
- Interpretation: No count in the facts isolates “ignored instructions” (care/washing, fit charts, return conditions, or promo terms) as its own category; the corpus cannot separate “explicitly ignored” from “unclear/missing instructions.”

In users' words
- “the exchange is so far effortless provided you do not loose the tags of the outfit” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]].
- “3 star is for most of the images not being the same as shown in pictures” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]].
- “I've even seen what looks like the exact same saree being sold by different verified pages for ₹400 and ₹1,500+, which makes me wonder what's actually going on.” [[rec|992e822486c366b967792807472aa652451ea1e2]].
- “Meesho is the worst place in terms of quality.” [[rec|9e2287759de3f3910bdcedd9edf57961b96c3556]].

Variation
- Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of which instructions (care, fit charts, return policies, promo terms) are ignored versus missing/hidden, nor on whether such discussion is concentrated in any particular source beyond the small late-revealed terms (D3) counts by source.

Counter-evidence
- Several rival barriers are also active: Fit & size uncertainty (C1) in 189 of 1,018 (share 0.186), Styling & self-image (C3) in 154 of 1,018 (share 0.151), External validation & social proof (C4) in 82 of 1,018 (share 0.081), External validation & social proof (C10) in 68 of 1,018 (share 0.067), and Intent extinguished after saving (C12) in 54 of 1,018 (share 0.053) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Barriers often co-occur: for example, the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) co-occurs with fulfilment (C7) in 65 joint records and with external validation & social proof (C4) in 53 joint records [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]].

Confidence
- Medium-Low. Price (C6) is reliable (kappa 0.645) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]], but the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) has weak agreement (kappa 0.427) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]], and fulfilment (C7) and late-revealed terms (D3) are not measurable for reliability [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|D3]]. Two validation thresholds fail at the corpus level [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. The topic of “ignoring instructions” is not directly coded, so findings are inferred from adjacent themes.

Limitations
- Every share is of discussion, not behavior; there is no funnel or conversion data here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow, with estimated recall near 45%, skewing away from some price/value and delivery/trust material; rankings are conditional on that rubric [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical takeaways rest on a smaller pool [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Agreement thresholds fail for some codes, and reliability for C7 and D3 is not measurable [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|D3]].
- App-store sources share a common skew; there are roughly three independent source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Counts below 30 are reportable but not rankable; late-revealed terms (D3) is thin and should not be over-interpreted [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Segments are derived, not observed; any lift into undecided groups is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of which instructions were ignored versus unclear/missing, nor on outcomes after ignoring (kept, returned, damaged, regret).
gate_reasons: the corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of what this is about
gate_caveats: whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for D3

results.question: What does the data say about disregarding the codebook?
results.restated: What does the analysed corpus indicate about whether we can ignore or discard the existing codebook (i.e. how much the data supports or contradicts disregarding the codebook)?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: Do not discard the codebook. Machine clusters align with key hand-coded barriers in multiple places, while a non-trivial Z‑99 residual exists and should be used to refine/extend the codebook rather than replace it.

Evidence
- What “disregarding the codebook” would mean operationally
  - Interpretation: Replacing hand codes with only machine-discovered clusters; or heavily merging/splitting codes around those clusters; or treating Z‑99 residuals as a new thematic set to drive coding.
- How much sits genuinely outside the codebook
  - A Z‑99 residual cluster contains 113 records out of 113 in the z99 space (code_size=116) [[analysis_cluster_code|z99|0|Z-99]].
  - Machine clusters with Z‑99 show up across the “all” space: cluster 13 (n=12 of 50), cluster 9 (n=11 of 42), cluster 14 (n=10 of 24), cluster 18 (n=7 of 36), and cluster 8 (n=6 of 45) [[analysis_cluster_code|all|13|Z-99]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|9|Z-99]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|14|Z-99]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|18|Z-99]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|8|Z-99]].
  - Z‑99 is discussed across sources: YouTube n=74/573 (share=0.129), Reddit n=32/309 (share=0.104), Play n=16/114 (share=0.14), App Store n=6/22 (share=0.273) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|play|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|Z-99]].
- Alignment between machine clusters and hand codes
  - Multiple clusters are dominated by the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2): cluster 15 (n=43 of 68), cluster 17 (n=26 of 42), cluster 11 (n=18 of 23), cluster 6 (n=16 of 30), cluster 10 (n=11 of 15), cluster 2 (n=10 of 157), cluster 16 (n=9 of 41), cluster 18 (n=8 of 36) [[analysis_cluster_code|all|15|C2]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|17|C2]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|11|C2]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|6|C2]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|10|C2]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|2|C2]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|16|C2]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|18|C2]].
  - External validation & social proof (C4) also appears as a dominant code in several clusters: cluster 2 (n=8 of 157), cluster 11 (n=7 of 23), cluster 16 (n=5 of 41), cluster 8 (n=4 of 45) [[analysis_cluster_code|all|2|C4]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|11|C4]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|16|C4]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|8|C4]].
  - Several clusters labeled by the machine suggest themes partly or fully outside the current codes, matching where Z‑99 is concentrated: “Asking for clothing item links” (cluster 13) aligns with Z‑99 in that cluster (n=12) [[cluster_labels|all|13]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|13|Z-99]]; “Asking for the product link” (cluster 14) aligns with Z‑99 there (n=10) [[cluster_labels|all|14]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|14|Z-99]]. Cluster 9 blends “Too expensive; returns/quality issues” with Z‑99 (n=11) and also some C2 (n=5), indicating divergence from a single hand code [[cluster_labels|all|9]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|9|Z-99]], [[analysis_cluster_code|all|9|C2]].
- Novel, reproducible themes the codebook may have missed
  - Z‑99 appears with multi-source support (YouTube, Reddit, Play, App Store) as shown above [[analysis_source_code|youtube|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|play|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|Z-99]].
  - Example residuals include difficulty finding “good options in shoes” and meta-requests about shopping annoyances and tooling requests, which do not map cleanly to existing codes [[rec|c16a154be6e73ee360d753e03657810828768b5d]], [[rec|71b49323bdf1fe903aceac3f1866f5a516c9f406]], [[rec|d25ff11e02e7bc5b0f26cf1c9ec917eb53deca6d]].
- Risks to accuracy/interpretability if we ignore the codebook
  - Agreement is below threshold for key codes: C2 has kappa=0.427 with a verdict of weak; C4 and Z‑99 are not measurable for reliability due to too few gold labels [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|Z-99]].
  - Two validation thresholds fail overall, and relevance recall is estimated at about 79% against an 85% threshold [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
  - Themes overlap materially: C2 co-occurs above chance with C4 (n_joint=53; lift=2.73), with C7 (n_joint=65; lift=1.961), and with C6 (n_joint=54; lift=1.102), so throwing out the human schema could reduce interpretability of multi-cause discussions [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C6]].

In users' words
- “At many places the product varies from the copy.” [[rec|ea187e430aa118d9a8b4eff2af931bdad3bc1b0a]]
- “see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]]
- “sizes r not available for many liked products” [[rec|76cfa2c5d02613b6e764266ecced8f879d02ac82]]
- “not many good options in shoes otherwise good app” [[rec|c16a154be6e73ee360d753e03657810828768b5d]]

Variation
- The gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) is discussed more on Reddit (n=104/309; share=0.337) than on YouTube (n=116/573; share=0.202) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]].
- Z‑99 is present across all four source types (YouTube, Reddit, Play, App Store), as shown in the source mix above [[analysis_source_code|youtube|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|play|Z-99]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|Z-99]].
- Interpretation: Beyond these, the brief does not provide segment-level or platform-specific divergences tied to “wishlist” behavior itself.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers also take substantial shares of discussion, indicating that multiple codebook themes matter:
  - Price (C6): n=207/1018; share=0.203 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1): n=189/1018; share=0.186 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]
  - Styling & self-image (C3): n=154/1018; share=0.151 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]
  - Fulfilment (C7): n=140/1018; share=0.138 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
  - External validation & social proof (C10): n=68/1018; share=0.067 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]]
- Co-occurrence shows codes rarely operate in isolation (e.g., C2 with C4 and C7 above), so substituting cluster-only themes could obscure overlapping concerns [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].

Confidence
